entities.summary: Polyxenidas the Rhodian, a skilled general and admiral, played a pivotal role in the Hellenistic period. Born in the Rhodian city-state, Polyxenidas's military prowess and strategic thinking caught the attention of Antiochus III the Great, who appointed him as his chief naval commander. Under Antiochus's patronage, Polyxenidas led several successful campaigns against the Ptolemaic Kingdom and the Seleucid Empire, cementing his reputation as one of the most feared and respected military leaders of his time. Despite his successes, Polyxenidas's service to Antiochus ultimately led to his exile from his native Rhodos, a fate that would serve as a cautionary tale for future generations of Greek naval commanders. In the centuries following his death, Polyxenidas's legacy would be remembered and reinterpreted by historians and scholars, who would continue to debate the complexities of Hellenistic politics and military strategy.
